An affidavit-in-opposition has been filed by the assessee respondent, wherein, it has been stated that section 29 has no manner of application in this case and furthermore the Sales Tax was assessed on 9.5.1968 for the assessment year ending on 30.6.63 and as such the notice, as well as the assessment were barred by limitation and the third ground taken in this affidavit-in-opposition against the application before us is that the machinery imported was exempted under Notification No. SRO 1302(k)/62 dated 5.12.1962. It has also been stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that the questions as framed, are not questions of law, but even if it is framed properly the order of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal is to be upheld. 

 11. The next question is the question of limitation. This limitation is to be seen in the Finance Ordinance of 1960. In clause (f) of section 7 of Finance Ordinance for the words "two years" of the date of, "the words" as in section 29 of the Sales Tax Act has been substituted with the words "four years of the end of the year in which the tax was payable on." This latter quoted portion has been substituted with the figure 5 years by the finance Act of 1974. Year has been defined in section 2clause (20) as a "financial year". The goods were admittedly imported on 9-2-63 and the tax was payable under Finance Ordinance of 1960, which has been amended. The provision of 2 'years' has been substituted by 'four years' which means that the assessment is to be completed by 30-6-67 counting four years from 1-7-68. The argument of Mr. Mozammel Haque Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate, on this score is obviously erroneous because of the meaning of the word 'year' as given in section 2, subsection (20). The Jaw that was available for assessing compensation was the Finance Ordinance, 1960 and not Finance Act, 1964. The Finance Act of 1964 replaced the word "four years'' with the words "five years", but the starting point of this, "five years" shall be from 1-7-67 and shall cover these cases which were imported after coming into operation of the Finance Act of 1964 as it has not been given retrospective effect.
